newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures close higher after holiday.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures close higher after holiday.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures closed higher as traders returned from holiday vacations to see much lower prices, market sources said Thursday.
"People came back from holidays and saw some values. January was over $20.00 per megawatt (MWh)" before Christmas, said one trader.
Higher daily cash market prices and firmer natural gas quotes also supported electricity futures, traders said.
"The higher gas had a carryover trend," said another trader.
He noted that January and February contracts "have been pushed down pretty low...we should have good support here or not much lower."
February California-Oregon border (COB) closed up 71 cents at $15.32 per megawatt hour (MWh), while March was up 50 cents at $13.90. Other active COB contracts were 25 to 70 cents higher.
February Palo Verde was up 83 cents at $16.63, while March closed 78 cents higher at $15.88. Other PV contracts settled 15 cents lower to 65 cents higher.
